title: Scenarios towards limiting global mean temperature increase below 1.5 °C
problem: The transition pathways required to limit global warming to 1.5°C as targeted by the Paris Agreement have not been extensively explored, making it challenging to understand which socio-economic and technological assumptions make this ambitious goal feasible versus unachievable.
method: The authors describe scenarios that limit end-of-century radiative forcing to 1.9 W m⁻², restricting median warming to below 1.5°C, by using six integrated assessment models and a simple climate model under five different Shared Socio-economic Pathways to account for varying socio-economic and technological assumptions.
task: The task is to describe scenarios that limit global mean temperature increase to below 1.5°C, using six integrated assessment models to explore transition pathways under different socio-economic, technological, and resource assumptions derived from the Shared Socio-economic Pathways (SSPs).
innovation: This paper presents a comprehensive multi-model set of scenarios that limit global warming to below 1.5°C, detailing the required energy and land-use transformations and assessing their feasibility across five different Shared Socio-economic Pathways (SSPs).

The set of modelling frameworks participating in this study represents an ensemble of opportunity. However, it nevertheless represents a wide variety of modelling approaches and model behaviour. Several different model types are represented, including Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) models, partial equilibrium models and hybrid models that combine a systems dynamics or a systems engineering model with a CGE (see Supplementary Table 1).
